title: Alternating Bits Check
description: Given a positive integer `n`, return `true` if its binary representation has alternating bits — meaning no two adjacent bits have the same value — and `false` otherwise. Leading zeros above the most significant set bit are ignored.
hints: What happens when you XOR `n` with `n >> 1` if all adjacent bits of `n` are different?
Every bit up to the MSB becomes `1`, which holds if and only if `(x & (x + 1)) == 0` where `x = n ^ (n >> 1)`.

examples.explanation: 5 in binary is 101, which strictly alternates.
7 in binary is 111, which has adjacent 1s.
11 in binary is 1011, which has adjacent 1s at the lowest two bits.
